prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules direct E3 ubiquitin ligases to chosen proteins, through heterobifunctional PROTACs and through the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: one prize part, B037, naming Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The scientific claim is a single chemical idea, that a designed small molecule can bring an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a protein it does not inhibit into one ternary complex and so convert drug action from occupancy into catalytic, event-driven removal. Its two strands, the PROTAC design concept and the cereblon mechanism that revealed how thalidomide-type glues act, both rest on induced proximity and on the physical chemistry of ternary-complex formation and cooperativity. The principle has been reproduced by many independent groups for over two decades and the glue strand already underlies approved medicines, so the concept is validated even though no bifunctional degrader is yet approved. After reading all eight round-1 statements, the breadth of support (all eight ranked it, six in the top three) is not what persuades me; what persuades me is that no opponent disputes the science, only the attribution and timing, and those costs seem to me smaller than the novelty and reach of the idea. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the heterobifunctional degrader, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, so the trio covers the founding act of each strand.
statement.case_against: Any trio leaves out Sakamoto (co-inventor of the first PROTAC), Ciulli (VHL ligands and the structural and cooperativity basis of ternary complexes), Gray, Ito and Kim, and a committee that cannot defend omitting Sakamoto from a PROTAC citation would have a real problem. The two strands have different histories, since lenalidomide worked clinically before its mechanism was known, so a single citation could look assembled to fit the three-name limit. No PROTAC is yet an approved drug, so the committee could be a few years early, and the chemistry-versus-drug-modality question is not fully answered. B005 is cleaner on attribution and maturity, though it sits close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.

responses.point: Chabes treats PROTACs and molecular glues as one idea, induced proximity to the ubiquitin system, and says a two-part prize (concept plus mechanism) is the honest fallback if omitting Sakamoto cannot be defended.
responses.response: I agree that the single-idea reading is defensible and it is why I keep one prize part, but I would not describe the strands as identical: the glue strand was an explanation of an old drug, not a design. I therefore want the citation to name cereblon explicitly, so that Handa's contribution is credited for what it was. A split into two parts would not help, because B037 is one shortlisted achievement and a two-part split would need a second, distinct ballot entry, which would also lead to a fourth name. I would rather accept the three-name cut and say openly that it omits Sakamoto and Ciulli than stretch the rule.

responses.point: Somfai names B005 as the safer choice if B037 is judged early, and he prefers Deshaies over Ciulli in the third slot because Crews and Deshaies made the founding heterobifunctional degrader.
responses.response: I agree with the Deshaies-over-Ciulli reasoning and now apply it to Sakamoto as well: the founding demonstration is a judgement call, but Crews and Deshaies carry the concept and Ciulli's VHL work refines a modality that already existed. On timing, my threshold is concrete: I would move to B005 if the committee concludes that the missing approval undermines the claim itself, not merely its clinical consequences. I do not think it does, because the glue branch already has approved drugs and the mechanism is settled. So I keep B037 first and B005 as my fallback.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B037 last, sees PROTAC concept and cereblon mechanism as different discoveries, and would rather wait for approved degraders and settled attribution than award on a pipeline.
responses.response: The attribution point is the strongest objection I have heard and I do not dismiss it. Where I differ is on approval as the test: the scientific claim, that E3 recruitment drives catalytic removal, is already established by cereblon-based glues that are in clinical use. Waiting for a bifunctional approval would also not settle the attribution, since Sakamoto and Ciulli would remain just as hard to place. I accept that if the committee cannot agree on any trio, your position and B005 are the fair outcome.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B016 (Car and Parrinello) for its two-name attribution and four decades of maturity, and suggests it could be paired with B060 within the three-person limit.
responses.response: I agree that B016 is the cleanest credit on the shortlist and that its science is not in doubt. I do not move to it because the 1998 and 2013 prizes have already drawn a line through computational chemistry, and because a pairing with B060 would join a methods prize to a base-editing part that several members, including Chabes and Somfai, find uncomfortably close to the 2020 CRISPR prize. I would not oppose B016 if the committee wants a pure methods prize, but I would put B005 ahead of it as a fallback because it has a direct effect on how chemists make molecules.

responses.point: Aili proposes B002 (Schultz, Chin) with B060 (Liu), and notes that a first regulatory approval of a degrader before the decision could change the maturity argument.
responses.response: The genetic code expansion case is strong and mature, but the round-1 exchange shows that attribution there is as unsettled as for B037, with Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama all argued for, and the two-part pairing carries the CRISPR-overlap objection for B060. That gives me no cleaner prize than B037. I agree with your point on approval: a first approved bifunctional degrader would strengthen the maturity case, but I do not think it is needed for the claim.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a trio that leaves out Sakamoto and Ciulli, and whether PROTACs and glues are better treated as one achievement or two.
Whether the lack of an approved bifunctional degrader makes this year early relative to B005; my threshold would be a judgement that the claim itself, not only its clinical payoff, is unproven.
Whether Kosugi and Migita precursor work and the 2010 prize overlap would weaken B005 enough to matter if it becomes the fallback.
My recollection of priority details is from memory and unverified.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B037 or the two named alternatives B005 and B024. I serve with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, an institutional tie but not a bar to voting, and neither has a documented tie to any credited person. My research (lipids, membranes, amyloid) is scientifically close to B024 and B055, which I do not rank first. I have no personal or institutional relationship with any credited person that my profile documents. Nothing in round 1 changes this disclosure.
